title: Background Reconciliation Pipeline Unhandled Rejection Crash
businessContext: A monthly B2B billing service processes 10,000 subscription invoices in the background. In production, an unexpected currency conversion API timeout crashes the entire Node process with unhandledRejection, causing half the billing run to be skipped without notifications.
problemStatement: The pipeline mixes raw Promise arrays with Promise.all() and forEach loops. When one invoice fails, unhandled rejections terminate the worker. Refactor the pipeline to process invoices using Promise.allSettled(), collect individual failures for retry queues, and ensure no unhandled promise rejections can crash the process.
constraints: A single failing invoice must not abort other invoices in the batch.
All failures must be categorized and logged with invoice ID and failure reason.
Must return an aggregate summary: { succeeded: number, failed: Array<{ id, error }> }.
candidateTasks: Explain why `Array.prototype.forEach` with an async callback fails to await promises.
Replace the approach with `Promise.allSettled()` or chunked concurrency.
Return a resilient structure `{ succeeded: number, failed: Array<{ id, reason }> }`.
hints: Array.forEach ignores the return value of its callback; it fires all async functions synchronously and does not wait.
Promise.allSettled() returns an array of objects describing the outcome of each promise (fulfilled or rejected).

testCases.name: Gracefully handles mixed success and failures
testCases.explanation: All invoices are evaluated and failures do not crash the batch.

alternativeApproaches: Sequential for-await-of loop with try/catch block if rate limits mandate serial execution.
Worker pool (e.g. p-limit or p-map) with concurrency of 10 to protect external billing gateway from rate limits.
commonMistakes: Using Promise.all() thinking it solves error handling; Promise.all fails fast on the very first rejection and aborts reporting on remaining items.
Putting try/catch around forEach: the synchronous try/catch finishes before the async promises even resolve.
